messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: autoscaler(pool: gpu-usw2-prod) reached configured max_nodes=32 at 2001234567. Queue length: 2.8k, avg latency 4.2s, 429 throttles increasing. Paging oncall: @Jordan

Jordan (oncall): seeing it, acknowledging. Jumping in.

Jordan (oncall): quick snapshot: gpu-pool current_nodes=32 (max), pods pending due to pod-anti-affinity + node-level limits. autoscaler attempted 3 scale actions in last 10m and hit cap. Requesting manual cap increase / rapid unblock.

Maya (sre): thanks. Can we confirm customer-facing 429s? Any high-priority customers affected?

Jordan (oncall): yes — internal metric shows 4 external tenants with >5% request errors. Support flagging a couple of high-usage accounts. Sam from Prod-eng looped in.

Sam (prod-eng): confirmed: Support portal reports spike in error reports. Likely caused by request queuing hitting the router throttles. We should raise cap to 48 temporarily, monitor, then plan a proper scale-policy tweak.

Alex (infra): before manual increase — quick safety checks: 1) available quota in account? 2) GPU inventory available in region? 3) any scheduled infra changes? I can check.

Alex (infra): running quick checks...
```bash
# check quota
gcloud compute regions describe us-west2 --project=redwood-inference
# check inventory (internal tool)
inventory-cli list --type=gpu --region=us-west-2 --status=available
```

Alex (infra): inventory shows 30 spare GPUs available in the region, account quota allows +20 nodes immediately. We can request temporary capacity bump but want ops approval for >40.

Maya (sre): given the customer impact, I support bump to 48 as emergency measure. We'll record it as an emergency manual scale, will need postmortem and change ticket.

Jordan (oncall): I'm going to request manual cap raise from the autoscale controller. Tagging infra for exec approve: @Alex please trigger manual override if you have approval.

Alex (infra): executing manual node ceiling change now. Command and audit note below.
```bash
# increase max nodes for pool
redwoodctl autoscale set --pool gpu-usw2-prod --max-nodes 48 --reason "emergency: sustained queue growth and customer 429s" --requested-by jordan
```
Audit note: ticket INC-2001 created for emergency cap raise.

DeployBot: Change applied: autoscaler.max_nodes updated 32 -> 48 by alex at 2001234635. Rolling evaluation started.

Jordan (oncall): scaling observed. New nodes are provisioning — currently 8 nodes provisioning, 4 warm, 28 total active. Queue length dropping from 2.8k -> 900 in ~3 min.

Maya (sre): good. Start gradual traffic validation: route 10% of affected tenants back, watch 429 rate. If stable, increase to 50% after 5m.

Sam (prod-eng): doing canary routing for tenant group A now.

Jordan (oncall): canary looks okay. 429s for group A went from 7% -> 0.4%. CPU/GPU utilization on new nodes ~35%.

Maya (sre): monitor for hot-sharding/pod churn. Also check KV cache misses — queue spikes often correlate to missing prefix cache on new nodes.

Jordan (oncall): observed increased cache misses on new pods. Triggered warm-up job to prepopulate common prefixes.

Jordan (oncall): running warm-up command:
```bash
kubectl exec -n infra cache-warm -- ./warm-prefixes --target=us-west-2 --pool=gpu
```

Alex (infra): warm-up started. Also adjusted podSpread/affinity in a quick patch to allow denser packing while we recover. Patch applied to replica set gpu-serving-v2.

DeployBot: rollout gpu-serving-v2 config patch initiated by alex. 3/3 pods updated without restarts.

Jordan (oncall): backlog now 900 -> 120 in next 6 minutes. Throttles falling. Customer error reports tapering.

Maya (sre): excellent. Delete emergency alarm that spams paging? Let's keep alert but lower severity.

Jordan (oncall): set incident status to "mitigated" but still monitoring for 30m. Notifying Support/CS for customer comms to affected tenants.

Sam (prod-eng): filing follow-up action: - revert temporary affinity changes after normalization, - add autoscaler policy to allow higher emergency burst, - add warm-start for common prefixes when scaling. I'll create a backlog ticket.

Alex (infra): we'll also file a quota/runbook note for faster capacity approvals. Need manual approval flow for >40 nodes.

Maya (sre): logging timeline and metrics snapshot to the incident ticket. Please paste the quick metrics for postmortem.

Jordan (oncall): metrics snapshot (at peak):
- queue_len: 2800
- 429_rate: 6.8%
- avg_latency: 4.2s
- nodes_active: 32
- nodes_provisioned_after_raise: 48
- time_to_partial_relief: ~6m

Jordan (oncall): last note — we did a manual cap raise because autoscaler respected configured max. Change of plan: will propose a new policy that allows emergency burst to 1.5x max when QPS delta > threshold and infra approves.

Maya (sre): agreed. Postmortem owners: Jordan (incident timeline), Alex (infra capacity + runbook), Sam (product/backlog). I'll draft initial postmortem and share in #postmortems.

Jordan (oncall): closing thread for live mitigation. Will update ticket INC-2001 with full notes and next steps. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:

IncidentBot: Incident updated: status=mitigated, incident_id=INC-2001, responders=[Jordan, Maya, Alex, Sam].
